questions.q: What distinguishes a Task from an Event?
options: A Task has a due date; an Event has a start and end time
A Task can never be marked complete
An Event can only be created by an admin
A Task is only visible to the record owner
questions.explain: A Task is a to-do with a single due date. An Event is scheduled time, with both a start and an end date/time.

questions.q: What does "Log a Call" actually create?
options: A new Case
An already-completed Task describing the call
A new Event scheduled for tomorrow
A Chatter post only
questions.explain: Log a Call is a shortcut that creates a Task that's already marked complete, with a description of the call.

options: A report showing only closed Opportunities
A setting in Object Manager
A type of custom object
The combined feed of Tasks, Events, and logged calls on a record
questions.explain: The Activity Timeline aggregates upcoming/overdue and past Tasks, Events, and logged calls for any record that supports Activities.

questions.q: On the New Event form, what fields capture when it happens?
options: Start date/time and End date/time
A single Due Date field
Only a Status field
A Priority dropdown
questions.explain: Unlike a Task's single due date, an Event's New form asks for both a Start and an End date and time.

questions.q: Which kinds of records can get an Activity Timeline?
options: Only Account records
Only custom objects, never standard ones
Many standard objects that support Activities, such as Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity, and Case
Only Task records themselves
questions.explain: Any record whose object supports Activities — including Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity, and Case — gets its own Activity Timeline.
